about: Airport database. airports: key = IATA code, value = the airport. sets: course sets in order; each panel is one state map and lists its codes.

sets.name: CT, DE, DC, ME, MD & MA

ACT.tip: A-C from wACo, then T for Texas.

ACV.label: Arcata
ACV.tip: A-C from ArCata, then V: “ArCata Vista.”

ADQ.tip: Kodiak is famous for its bears: “Alaska's Den Queen.”

AKN.tip: A-K for AlasKa, then N from King salmoN.

ATW.tip: A-T from AppleTon, then W for Wisconsin.

ATY.tip: A-T from wATertown, then Y: “wATertown, Yes.”

AVP.label: Scranton
AVP.tip: The airport is in Avoca, PA: A-V from AVoca, then P for Pennsylvania.

BDL.label: Hartford
BDL.tip: Hartford's airport is Bradley International: B-D-L from BraDLey.

BKW.tip: B-K from BecKley, then W for West Virginia.

BKX.tip: B-K from BrooKings, then X marks the spot.

BNA.tip: Nashville's airport was Berry Field: B, then N-A from NAshville.

BQK.tip: B from Brunswick, then Q-K: “Brunswick's Quiet Keys.”

BTM.tip: B-T from BuTte, then M for Montana.

BTV.tip: B-T from BurlingTon, then V for Vermont.

CAE.tip: C-A from ColumbiA, then E: “Columbia's Always Exciting.”

CGX.label: Meigs
CGX.tip: C-G from ChicaGo, then X: Meigs Field is crossed out with an X because it closed in 2003.
CGX.clue: ChicaGo, crossed out with an X

CIU.label: Sault Ste Marie
CIU.tip: Sault Ste. Marie's airport is Chippewa County International: C-I-U from ChIppewa coUnty.

CLM.tip: Port Angeles is in Clallam County: C-L-M from CLallaM.

CMH.tip: C-M from CoLuMbus, then H from oHio.

CMX.tip: Hancock is in Michigan's Copper Country: “Copper Mine X.”

CNK.tip: C-N from CoNcordia, then K for Kansas.

CNM.tip: C from Carlsbad, then N-M for New Mexico.

CNY.tip: Moab's airport is Canyonlands Field: C-N-Y from CaNYonlands.

COD.tip: Just the first three letters: COD-y.

CPR.tip: Take the C, P and R from CasPeR and skip the other letters. They spell CPR, like the first aid. Picture a cowboy getting CPR in Casper.

CRW.tip: C-R from ChaRleston, then W for West Virginia.

CSG.tip: C-S from ColumbuS, then G for Georgia.

CVN.tip: C-V from CloVis, then N for New Mexico.

CYS.tip: C and Y come from CheYenne. For the S, think “State capital,” because Cheyenne is Wyoming’s capital city. Say it: “Capital? Yes, Sir!” C, Y, S.

DAL.label: Love Field
DAL.tip: Just the first three letters of Dallas: DAL. This is Love Field, the smaller airport. The big one is DFW (Dallas/Fort Worth).

DCA.label: National
DCA.tip: Washington National is the D.C. Airport: D-C-A.

DFW.label: Dallas/Fort Worth
DFW.tip: D, F and W are the first letters of Dallas/Fort Worth. This is the big airport; the smaller one, Love Field, is DAL.

DUJ.tip: D-U from DUbois, then J: “DUbois Jets.”

EWR.tip: E, W and R are inside nEWaRk, in order. Newark is in New Jersey, across the river from New York’s JFK and LGA.

FCA.tip: Kalispell's airport began as Flathead County Airport: F-C-A.

FOE.tip: Topeka's airport was Forbes Field: F-O-E from FOrbEs.

GCC.tip: Only the G is in the name. For the rest, think of Gillette razors: “Gillette Cuts Clean.” G, C, C.

GEG.tip: Spokane's airport was Geiger Field: G-E-G from GEiGer.

GLH.tip: G-L from GreenviLle, then H: “GreenviLle Harbor.”

GPZ.tip: G from Grand Rapids, then P-Z: “Grand Pines Zone” (Minnesota north woods).

GTR.tip: Columbus, MS is served by Golden Triangle Regional: G-T-R.

GUC.tip: G-U from GUnnison, then C for Colorado.

GYY.tip: G from Gary, then Y-Y: “Gary? Yes, Yes!”

HAE.tip: H-A from HAvasupai, then E: “Havasupai: Always Exploring.”

HII.label: Lake Havasu
HII.tip: “Havasu Is Incredible.” H from Havasu, I, I.

HOU.label: Hobby
HOU.tip: Just the first three letters of Houston: HOU. This is Hobby, the smaller airport. The big one is IAH.

HPN.label: Westchester
HPN.tip: Westchester County Airport is in White Plains: wHite PlaiNs.

HUF.tip: Terre Haute's airport is Hulman Field: H-U-F from HUlman Field.

IAD.label: Dulles
IAD.tip: Dulles was going to be DIA, but that looked too much like DCA, so the letters were shuffled: I-A-D.

IFP.label: Bullhead City
IFP.tip: Bullhead City sits across the river from Laughlin's casinos: “I Feel Prosperous.”

ITO.label: Hilo
ITO.tip: The Big Island is nicknamed the Orchid Isle: “Island of The Orchids.”

JAC.tip: Just the first three letters: JAC-kson Hole.

JAX.tip: J-A from JAcksonville, then X like LAX.

JFK.label: JFK Kennedy
JFK.tip: Named for President John F. Kennedy: J-F-K.

JGC.label: GC Heliport
JGC.tip: Jet-copter to Grand Canyon: J, then G-C for Grand Canyon.

JHM.label: Kapalua
JHM.tip: “Just Hawaii, Maui.” Kapalua is on Maui.

JHW.tip: J from Jamestown, then H-W: “Jamestown Heads West” (it's in western New York).

LAR.tip: Just the first three letters: LAR-amie.

LAX.tip: LA plus X. When codes went from two letters to three, Los Angeles added an X.

LBF.tip: North Platte's airport is Lee Bird Field: L-B-F.

LGA.label: LaGuardia
LGA.tip: L, G and A are inside LaGuArdia, in order. New York also has JFK, and Newark (EWR) is just across the river.

LNK.tip: L-N from LiNcoln, then K: say it “LiNK.”

LYU.tip: L-Y from eLY, then U: “eLY, yoU.”

MBL.tip: Manistee's airport is Manistee County-Blacker: M, then B-L from BLacker.

MBS.label: Saginaw
MBS.tip: The airport serves three cities: Midland, Bay City, Saginaw.

MCI.tip: Kansas City's airport was Mid-Continent International: M-C-I.

MCO.label: Orlando Intl
MCO.tip: Orlando International used to be McCoy Air Force Base: M-C-O from MCcOy.

MCW.tip: Mason City, then W: “Mason City Wins.”

MDH.tip: Carbondale is home to the SIU Salukis, a dog breed: “Many Dawgs Here.”

MDJ.tip: M-D from MaDras, then J: “MaDras Junction.”

MDT.tip: Harrisburg International is in Middletown: M-D-T from MiDdleTown.

MDW.label: Midway
MDW.tip: M, D and W are inside MiDWay, in order. Chicago’s bigger airport is O’Hare, ORD.

MFE.label: McAllen
MFE.tip: M from McAllen, then F-E: “McAllen Fiesta Everyday.”

MHK.tip: M-H from ManHattan, then K for Kansas.

MKK.label: Hoolehua
MKK.tip: M-K from MoloKai, then say the K twice: M-K-K.

MKL.tip: Jackson, TN's airport is McKellar-Sipes: M-K-L from McKelLar.

MLU.tip: M from Monroe, then L-U from LoUisiana.

MSY.tip: New Orleans’ airport was built on the old Moisant Stock Yards: M-S-Y.

MTJ.tip: M-T from MonTrose, then J: “MonTrose Jets.”

MWA.tip: Marion's airport is Williamson County: M, then W-A for Williamson Airport.

OAJ.tip: Jacksonville, NC is in Onslow County and its airport is Albert J. Ellis: O-A-J.

OAK.tip: Just the first three letters of Oakland: OAK. It is across the bay from San Francisco, SFO.

OGG.label: Kahului
OGG.tip: Named for pilot Bertram Hogg: h-O-G-G.

ORD.label: O'Hare
ORD.tip: O'Hare used to be Orchard Field: O-R-D from ORcharD.

ORH.tip: Worcester is the city of seven hills: O-R from wORcester, H for Hills.

PAE.tip: Everett's airport is Paine Field: P-A-E from PAinE.

PAK.label: Hanapepe
PAK.tip: The airport is Port Allen, on Kauai: P-A from Port Allen, K for Kauai.

PDX.tip: P-D from PortlanD, then X like LAX.

PFN.tip: P from Panama, then F-N: “Panama, Florida, Now.”

PGA.tip: P-G from PaGe, then A for Arizona.

PGV.tip: The airport is Pitt-Greenville: P-G-V from Pitt-GreenVille.

PHF.label: Newport News
PHF.tip: The Newport News airport was Patrick Henry Field: P-H-F.

PIB.tip: Laurel is in the Pine Belt region: P-I-B from PIne Belt.

PIE.label: Clearwater
PIE.tip: St. Pete-Clearwater is in Pinellas County: P-I from PInellas, easy as PIE.

PIH.tip: Pocatello, Idaho: P, then I-H from IdaHo.

PUW.tip: P-U from PUllman, then W for Washington.

PWM.tip: P from Portland, then W-M: “Portland, Wonderful Maine.”

RIW.tip: R-I from RIverton, but it is not RIV: it ends in W. Picture “Riverton’s Icy Wind.” R, I, W.

RKS.tip: Think of the word ROCKS and take out the O and the C. What’s left is R, K, S.
RKS.clue: ROCKS without the O and C

RSJ.tip: R-S from RoSario, then J for the San Juan Islands, where Rosario is.

RSW.tip: Fort Myers' airport started as Regional SouthWest: R-S-W.

SCC.label: Prudhoe Bay
SCC.tip: Prudhoe Bay is oil country on the North Slope: “Slope Crude Center.”

SDF.tip: Louisville's airport was Standiford Field: S-D-F from StanDiford Field.

SHD.label: Staunton
SHD.tip: Staunton is in the Shenandoah Valley: S-H-D from SHenanDoah.

SHR.tip: Picture the SHeRiff of SHeRidan: S, H, R. Take the S and H, then jump ahead to the R.

SJT.tip: S from San Angelo, then J-T: “San Angelo, Just Texas.”

SMX.tip: Santa Maria: S-M, then X like LAX.

SPS.tip: Wichita Falls shares its field with Sheppard Air Force Base: “SheP-pard Skies.”

SRQ.tip: S-R from SaRasota, then Q: “SaRasota's Quiet beaches.”

STL.tip: St. is short for Saint: S-T from St., then L from Louis. STL.

TBN.label: Ft Leonard Wood
TBN.tip: The airport serves the Army post: “Troops' Base Nearby.”

TEX.tip: T-E from TElluride, then X: “Telluride EXtreme” skiing.

TSM.tip: T-S from TaoS, then M for (New) Mexico.

TYS.tip: Knoxville's airport is McGhee Tyson: T-Y-S from TYSon.

WDG.tip: Enid's airport is Woodring Regional: W-D-G from WooDrinG.

WMH.tip: W, then M-H for Mountain Home: “Welcome, Mountain Home.”

WRL.tip: Take the vowels out of “WoRLd” and you get WRL. Worland starts the same way: W-o-R-L-and.

WSX.tip: W-S from WestSound, then X: “WestSound eXpress,” like its ferries.

XNA.place: Bentonville / Fayetteville - NW Arkansas Regional, AR
XNA.label: Bentonville (XNA)
XNA.tip: X, then N-A for Northwest Arkansas.

ZRF.label: Rockford P&R Bus
ZRF.tip: Bus and train stops get Z codes: Z, then R-F from RockFord.

ZRK.label: Rockford VG Bus
ZRK.tip: Z for bus, then R-K from RocKford (the Van Galder bus).
